questions.consigne: Ex. I — Complete the conversations. Put in the correct form of each verb. Use the present continuous or the present simple.
questions.enonce:
A: _____ (I / think) of buying a new computer.
B: But computers **cost** so much money. What's wrong with the one we've got?
A: **It's getting** out of date now.
questions.explication: « think of + -ing » = envisager : c'est une activité mentale en cours, pas une opinion → present continuous.

questions.consigne: Ex. I — Complete the conversations. Put in the correct form of each verb. Use the present continuous or the present simple.

B: But computers _____ (cost) so much money. What's wrong with the one we've got?
A: **It's getting** out of date now.
questions.explication: Fait général ou habitude → present simple.

questions.consigne: Ex. I — Complete the conversations. Put in the correct form of each verb. Use the present continuous or the present simple.

questions.consigne: Ex. I — Complete the conversations. Put in the correct form of each verb. Use the present continuous or the present simple.

questions.consigne: Ex. I — Complete the conversations. Put in the correct form of each verb. Use the present continuous or the present simple.

questions.consigne: Ex. I — Complete the conversations. Put in the correct form of each verb. Use the present continuous or the present simple.

questions.explication: B répond « I'm weighing this letter » : A demande ce qu'il est en train de faire → present continuous. (La fiche corrigée donne « do you do », mais ça demande le métier ; les deux sont acceptés.)

questions.explication: weigh = peser, c'est ici une action, en cours maintenant → present continuous.

questions.consigne: Ex. I — Complete the conversations. Put in the correct form of each verb. Use the present continuous or the present simple.

A: About ten o'clock usually. But **it doesn't make** any difference.

questions.consigne: Ex. III — Some of these sentences are correct, and some have a word which should not be there. If the sentence is correct, write « ok ». If it is incorrect, write the unnecessary have or has.
questions.enonce: The directors have arrived half an hour ago, but they didn't stay long. → _____ (ok / have / has)
questions.explication: « half an hour ago » : ago = moment précis du passé → past simple : « The directors arrived… ».

questions.consigne: Ex. III — Some of these sentences are correct, and some have a word which should not be there. If the sentence is correct, write « ok ». If it is incorrect, write the unnecessary have or has.
questions.enonce: It's raining, and Peter has left his umbrella behind, look. → _____ (ok / have / has)
questions.explication: Correct : résultat présent (il n'a pas son parapluie maintenant, « look ») → present perfect.

questions.consigne: Ex. III — Some of these sentences are correct, and some have a word which should not be there. If the sentence is correct, write « ok ». If it is incorrect, write the unnecessary have or has.
questions.enonce: It's a long time since your friends have last visited us. → _____ (ok / have / has)
questions.explication: « It's a long time since + past simple » : since your friends last visited us.

questions.consigne: Ex. III — Some of these sentences are correct, and some have a word which should not be there. If the sentence is correct, write « ok ». If it is incorrect, write the unnecessary have or has.
questions.enonce: None of you have called me for weeks. Aren't we friends any more? → _____ (ok / have / has)
questions.explication: Correct : « for weeks » jusqu'à maintenant → present perfect.

questions.consigne: Ex. III — Some of these sentences are correct, and some have a word which should not be there. If the sentence is correct, write « ok ». If it is incorrect, write the unnecessary have or has.
questions.enonce: We can play tennis now. The others have finished. → _____ (ok / have / has)
questions.explication: Correct : résultat présent (le court est libre maintenant) → present perfect.

questions.consigne: Ex. III — Some of these sentences are correct, and some have a word which should not be there. If the sentence is correct, write « ok ». If it is incorrect, write the unnecessary have or has.
questions.enonce: The company has bought some land, but then it sold it. → _____ (ok / have / has)
questions.explication: La suite (« but then it sold it ») raconte un passé terminé : « The company bought some land… » → past simple.

questions.consigne: Ex. III — Some of these sentences are correct, and some have a word which should not be there. If the sentence is correct, write « ok ». If it is incorrect, write the unnecessary have or has.
questions.enonce: The computer isn't on now. Someone has turned it off. → _____ (ok / have / has)
questions.explication: Correct : résultat présent (il est éteint maintenant) → present perfect.

questions.consigne: Ex. III — Some of these sentences are correct, and some have a word which should not be there. If the sentence is correct, write « ok ». If it is incorrect, write the unnecessary have or has.
questions.enonce: Tessa has posted the parcel. It's on its way to you. → _____ (ok / have / has)

questions.consigne: Ex. III — Some of these sentences are correct, and some have a word which should not be there. If the sentence is correct, write « ok ». If it is incorrect, write the unnecessary have or has.
questions.enonce: Several bombs have gone off in the city centre. It has happened an hour ago. → _____ (ok / have / has)
questions.explication: « an hour ago » → past simple : « It happened an hour ago ».

questions.consigne: Ex. III — Some of these sentences are correct, and some have a word which should not be there. If the sentence is correct, write « ok ». If it is incorrect, write the unnecessary have or has.
questions.enonce: Simon has left. He and Oliver have left after lunch. → _____ (ok / have / has)
questions.explication: « after lunch » = moment précis → « He and Oliver left after lunch » (past simple).

questions.consigne: Ex. IV — Put in the present perfect or past simple of the verbs in brackets.
questions.enonce: The last time I _____ (go) to Brighton was in August.
questions.explication: « The last time… was in August » : moment précis du passé → past simple.

questions.consigne: Ex. IV — Put in the present perfect or past simple of the verbs in brackets.
questions.enonce: I'd like to meet a ghost, but I _____ (never / see) one.
questions.explication: never = jamais de toute ma vie (expérience jusqu'à maintenant) → present perfect.

questions.consigne: Ex. IV — Put in the present perfect or past simple of the verbs in brackets.

questions.consigne: Ex. IV — Put in the present perfect or past simple of the verbs in brackets.

questions.consigne: Ex. IV — Put in the present perfect or past simple of the verbs in brackets.
questions.enonce: What time _____ (you / get) to work this morning?

questions.consigne: Ex. IV — Put in the present perfect or past simple of the verbs in brackets.
questions.enonce: Martin _____ (be) to Greece five times. He loves the place.

questions.consigne: Ex. IV — Put in the present perfect or past simple of the verbs in brackets.
questions.enonce: The President _____ (come) out of the building and is going to make a speech.

questions.consigne: Ex. IV — Put in the present perfect or past simple of the verbs in brackets.

questions.consigne: Ex. IV — Put in the present perfect or past simple of the verbs in brackets.
questions.enonce: Of course I can ride a bike. But I _____ (not / ride) one for years.

questions.consigne: Ex. IV — Put in the present perfect or past simple of the verbs in brackets.

questions.consigne: Ex. IV — Put in the present perfect or past simple of the verbs in brackets.
questions.enonce: Janet _____ (be) very ill three years ago.

questions.consigne: Ex. IV — Put in the present perfect or past simple of the verbs in brackets.

questions.consigne: Ex. IV — Put in the present perfect or past simple of the verbs in brackets.

questions.consigne: Ex. IV — Put in the present perfect or past simple of the verbs in brackets.
